findings.title: Raw recovery codes sent to user storage as credential value
findings.body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` serializes the plaintext generated codes to JSON and passes them to `updateCredential`. Any user storage provider that supports the recovery-codes type therefore receives the raw, unhashed codes. The local path stores hashed codes via the credential model. This is inconsistent and leaves the secrets in plaintext. The test provider also validates by comparing the plaintext codes.

findings.title: Credential lookup order and removal ignore federated credentials
findings.body: `getCredential` can now return a federated credential. In `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`, `allCodesUsed()` leads to `removeStoredCredentialById`, which only removes local credentials. A federated credential is never removed or updated when codes are used. Used codes are also never marked used in the federated store, so the next-code number never advances.

findings.title: Test storage returns inconsistent recovery credential model
findings.body: `getCredentials` rebuilds the model with `createFromValues` on the raw codes. That generates a new credential without the stored id, so the id differs from the stored one. The raw codes are hashed into the credential data, which is inconsistent with the storage's `isValid` that compares plaintext. `getCredentials` also does not null-check `myUser`, unlike other methods, so it throws an NPE for an unknown user.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get()
findings.body: `credentialModelOpt.get()` throws NoSuchElementException if no credential is found. Before this change the code had the same `.get()` on a stream. With the federated lookup, a storage that reports `isConfiguredFor` but returns no credential from `getFederatedCredentialsStream` triggers the exception. Handle the empty case explicitly.
